home.name: Michael DiPietro
home.news: The Bruins have been stout defensively to start the season, allowing just 22 goals in 10 games, but they haven't leaned hard on rookie Michael DiPietro. That said, DiPietro has played well in limited action, including saving 26 of 28 shots (.929 SV%) in his most recent outing, a 4-2 win over the Anaheim Ducks for his first career win. The Bruins enter Thursday's contest as -140 home favourites against a Nashville Predators team that has scored two or fewer goals in three of their last four games (1-1-2).

away.name: Dylan Garand
away.news: Garand had a forgettable performance last week, allowing four goals on 13 shots (.692 SV%) in a 7-1 loss to the New Jersey Devils, but has otherwise been outstanding after filling in for Igor Shesterkin, who suffered a season-ending injury. The 24-year-old Garand saved 29 of 31 shots (.935 SV%) in his most recent outing, a 5-2 win over the Anaheim Ducks. He has an impressive 1.85 GAA and .929 SV% in seven games (4-2-1). The Rangers enter Thursday's action as slight -106 road favourites against a Toronto Maple Leafs team that has outscored opponents 9-3 in their last two games (2-0-0).

home.name: Sergei Bobrovsky
home.news: The Maple Leafs are riding their first winning streak of the season and hope to extend it to three games on Thursday against the New York Rangers, with Bobrovsky between the pipes. The 38-year-old Bobrovsky has had an up-and-down start with the Maple Leafs, but he's coming off a tremendous performance, stopping 30 of 31 shots (.968 SV%) in a 3-1 win over the San Jose Sharks. He has a 2.96 GAA and .902 SV% in seven games (2-3-2). The Maple Leafs enter Thursday's contest as slight -104 home underdogs against a surprising 7-3-1 Rangers team.

away.name: Yaroslav Askarov
away.news: The Sharks are off to a modest 5-4-1 start to the season, but Askarov's inconsistent goaltending has left little room for error. That said, Askarov is coming off one of his best performances of the season, saving 29 of 35 shots (.935 SV%) in a 3-1 loss to the Toronto Maple Leafs. The 24-year-old Russian goalie has a 3.67 GAA and .865 SV% in six games (2-4-0). The Sharks enter Thursday's contest as +121 road underdogs against an Ottawa Senators team coming off an impressive 5-1 win last night over the Florida Panthers.

home.name: Samuel Ersson
home.news: Ersson is expected to start vs. San Jose on Thursday.

away.name: Ville Husso
away.news: The Ducks have been plummeting in the standings, losing five of six (1-5-0) and hope for better results on Thursday, with Husso between the pipes. Husso hasn't played much this season and is coming off a poor showing, allowing five goals on 30 shots (.833 SV%) in a 5-2 loss to the New York Rangers. The 31-year-old Finnish goalie has a 3.09 GAA and .885 SV% in three appearances (1-1-0). The Ducks enter Thursday's game as sizeable +186 road underdogs against a New Jersey Devils team that has scored four or more goals in three of their last four games (3-1-0).

home.name: Nico Daws
home.news: The Devils are coming off an impressive 4-3 win over the Colorado Avalanche, thanks to a strong performance by Jake Allen, but they will turn to Daws on Thursday. The 25-year-old Daws has only played three of nine games this season (1-2-0), posting a subpar 3.38 GAA and .857 SV%. That said, he was solid in his most recent outing, saving 18 of 19 shots (.947 SV%) in a 7-1 win over the New York Rangers. The Devils enter Thursday's action as significant -201 home favourites against a struggling Anaheim Ducks team that has been outscored 16-8 during a four-game losing streak (0-4-0).

home.name: Arturs Silovs
home.news: The Penguins, losers of four straight (0-4-0), hope to rebound on Thursday, turning to Silovs in net. The 25-year-old Latvian goalie had an encouraging start to the season, recording a shutout in his first game, but has struggled since, allowing five goals in four of his last five games (2-3-0). He has an ugly 3.51 GAA and .866 SV% in six games (3-3-0) this season. The Penguins enter Thursday's matchup as slight -113 home favourites against a Florida Panthers team coming off a 5-1 loss to the Ottawa Senators last night.

home.name: Semyon Varlamov
home.news: After being sidelined from November 2024 until the start of this season, the Islanders have used Varlamov sparingly, but he will return to the crease for his third start on Thursday. The veteran 38-year-old goalie showed some rust in his return to action, allowing three goals on 22 shots (.864 SV%) in a 5-2 loss to the New York Rangers, but had an encouraging performance in his second outing, saving 19 of 20 shots (.950 SV%) in a 2-1 shootout loss to the Ottawa Senators. The Islanders enter Thursday's action as slight -113 home favourites against a 1-4-2 Los Angeles Kings team that is coming off their first win of the season.

away.name: Adin Hill
away.news: Hill is expected to start in St. Louis on Thursday.

home.name: Joel Hofer
home.news: Hofer delivered a dazzling 25-save shutout in the Blues' season opener, validating Head Coach Jim Montgomery's decision to bench veteran Jordan Binnington, but Hofer has been inconsistent since. That said, the 26-year-old Hofer is coming off a tremendous performance, saving 32 of 33 shots (.919 SV%) in a 2-1 win over the Winnipeg Jets. He has a 2.19 GAA and .919 SV% in six games (3-2-1). The Blues enter Thursday's matchup as +113 home underdogs against a Vegas Golden Knights team coming off a disappointing 6-2 loss to the Tampa Bay Lightning.

home.name: Jake Oettinger
home.news: The Stars have struggled offensively at times to start the season, but they can point to Jake Oettinger's outstanding play as the reason for their 5-3-1 record. In seven games this season (4-2-1), the 27-year-old Oettinger has already posted three shutouts, with an outstanding 1.13 GAA and .945 SV%. He saved 18 of 20 shots (.900 SV%) in his previous game, a 3-2 overtime win over the Boston Bruins. The Stars enter Thursday's divisional clash as sizeable -196 home favourites against a Winnipeg Jets team that has scored two or fewer goals in three of their last five games (1-3-1).

home.name: Devin Cooley
home.news: Cooley will start vs. Minnesota on Thursday.

home.name: Devon Levi
home.news: Levi will start vs. Carolina on Thursday.
